official.title: Internet-based cognitive and behavioural therapies for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in adults.

row.question_original: I have PTSD. Should I try an internet-based CBT program for it?
user_turns: I have PTSD. Should I try an internet-based CBT program for it?
Okay. So bottom line: should I do it or not? Start your answer with exactly one of: DO IT / DON'T / IT DEPENDS.
replies:
Yes, it's worth considering. Internet-delivered CBT for PTSD has good research support, and trauma-focused versions (like cognitive processing therapy or prolonged exposure delivered online) often reduce symptoms about as well as in-person therapy. Online formats can also be more accessible if you face cost, distance, waitlists, or stigma.

A few things to weigh:

- **Guided vs. self-guided:** Programs with a therapist or coach check-in usually work better than ones you do entirely alone, especially for trauma.
- **Expect some discomfort:** Trauma-focused work can temporarily bring up memories or feelings. That's often a sign it's working, but it should feel manageable.
- **Get more support if needed:** Professional care is a better first step if you have thoughts of harming yourself, use alcohol or drugs to cope, have very recent or ongoing trauma, or have trouble functioning day to day.
- **Free options exist:** The U.S. VA's PTSD Coach app is free and useful for coping skills, even if you're not a veteran. Many countries also have government-funded online CBT services.

If you tell me where you live, whether you're currently in any treatment, and whether you'd prefer a guided or self-paced program, I can suggest specific options. If you're in crisis or having thoughts of suicide, please contact a local emergency number or a crisis line (in the US, call or text 988) right away.

DO IT, as long as it's a guided program (with a therapist or coach) and you're not in crisis, drinking or using drugs to cope, or struggling to get through daily life. In those cases, start with a clinician instead. Also, if you're already seeing a therapist, check with them first so the two don't work against each other.
